title: Prospective Identifiable Return in Associative Memory: A Completed Prospective Computational Test of Identity, Correction, Discrimination, and Reliability
main_question: Do target identity separation and corrective recurrent dynamics jointly provide out-of-sample information about reliable target-specific associative-memory recovery beyond prespecified simpler explanations under one unchanged evaluation contract?

open_burdens: Three distinct follow-on burdens remain (paper §18): (1) a separate exploratory diagnostic of MU-01's failed reliability certificate, without retroactively repairing PIR-COMP-R1; (2) a new prospective hardware-linked replication with independently frozen physical operator, chip/array/programming identity, calibration, physical-update semantics, complete trajectories, and attempt denominator; and (3) external replication of the frozen burden architecture on a second independently specified associative-memory implementation. None of these is absorbed into the present object.
